# Adjudication Task — Chapter 984

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃984화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|발 없는 말이 천 리를 간다는 속담은 틀렸다. 만 리, 아니 더 멀리도 눈 깜짝할 사이에 갈 수 있다.
  6|
  7|북방을 중심으로 벌어진 일련의 사건들은 놀라울 정도로 빠르게, 더불어 끝없이 퍼져 나갔다.
  8|
  9|사람들의 입에서 입으로, 전서응의 날갯짓으로, 전령(傳令)들의 바쁜 채찍질을 따라 힘차게 내달리는 말발굽으로.
 10|
 11|그리고 밝혀진 진실에 대한 여파는, 이내 중원 전체를 뒤흔들기에 충분했다.
 12|
 13|“모용세가가 어찌……!”
 14|
 15|“말도 안 돼. 그럴 리가 없소!”
 16|
 17|처음 소식을 접한 무림인들이 드러낸 감정은 바로 불신이었다.
 18|
 19|당연한 일이었다.
 20|
 21|만천하에 드러난 배신자들의 정체는 장강수로맹이나 녹림맹처럼 사마외도(邪魔外道)에 뿌리를 둔 집단이 아닌, 무려 모용세가였으니까.
 22|
 23|천하 오대 세가의 일원.
 24|
 25|비록 북방의 끝자락이라고는 하나, 광활한 면적을 지닌 요녕땅을 넘어 중원에 이르기까지 그 명성을 모르는 이가 없는 말 그대로의 세가(世家).
 26|
 27|그런데 바로 그 모용세가가 암천과 손을 잡았다고 했다.
 28|
 29|심지어 몇몇 불순분자의 소행도 아닌, 가주인 모용백을 포함한 가문원 대부분이.
 30|
 31|그렇기에 이 믿을 수 없는 소식을 접한 사람들이 받은 충격은 말로 형용할 수 없을 정도였다.
 32|
 33|“가주인 이룡신창(螭龍神槍)은 정마대전에서도 혁혁한 공을 세웠던 인물이오. 그런 그가, 모용세가가 도대체 무슨 연유로…….”
 34|
 35|하지만 그들이 느낀 불신은 찰나에 불과했다.
 36|
 37|개방이, 하오문이, 화산파와 하북팽가가.
 38|
 39|그리고 천하 무림의 중심이라 할 수 있는 무림맹이 공식적으로 모든 것이 한 치의 거짓도 없는 사실을 밝혔기 때문이었다.
 40|
 41|심지어는, 존재하되 존재하지 않는 것과 같았던 무림 밖의 거인까지도.
 42|
 43|“길을 여시오!”
 44|
 45|적게는 수십, 많게는 수백에 달하는 관병들이 무리 지어 곳곳을 누볐다.
 46|
 47|길어진 평화 속 나른한 얼굴로 창에 기대어 하루를 보내던 그들은, 철저한 무장을 갖춘 채 투구 사이로 한껏 날카로워진 눈매로 사방을 주시하며 자신들에게 떨어진 명령을 수행했다.
 48|
 49|“여보게, 무슨 일인가?”
 50|
 51|“글쎄. 난들 알 턱이 있나. 다만 분위기가 흉흉한 걸 보니 근래에 황도(皇都)에서 벌어졌다는 모종의 사건에 관한 문제가 아닐까 싶은데.”
 52|
 53|“어, 나도 그 소식 들었네. 암천인지 뭔지 그 쳐죽일 놈들 말하는 거 맞나? 아는 무림인한테 듣기로는 놈들이 또 한 번 난동을 피웠다는데…….”
 54|
 55|그것은 비단 어느 한 곳에서만 벌어지는 일이 아니었다.
 56|
 57|갑작스럽게 돌변한 관병들의 모습을 본 사람들은 당혹스러움과 긴장감을 동시에 느끼며 모여들었다.
 58|
 59|그리고 머지않아 관병들이 사방에 붙이고 떠난 방(榜)의 내용을 확인할 수 있었다.
 60|
 61|
 62|
 63|만천하, 만백성에게 고하노라.
 64|
 65|
 66|
 67|각 성부에 속한 문장가들이 일필휘지(一筆揮之)로 써내려 간 포고문의 첫 문장은 그렇게 시작되었고, 수많은 군중들의 시선을 받아 떠밀리듯 앞으로 나선 유생들의 목소리는 시간이 흐를수록 잘게 떨렸다.
 68|
 69|“……하, 하여 관에 속하지 않은 무부(武夫)들을 아울러 암천(暗天)이라 불리는 역적의 무리를 일벌백계하고자 하니, 이는 곧 짐의 뜻이자 하늘의 계시로다.”
 70|
 71|제법 긴 낭송을 끝마친 후에도 장내는 쥐죽은 듯이 조용했다.
 72|
 73|이 갑작스러운 포고문에 대한 뜻을 이해한 이들은 유생들과 같이 눈을 부릅떴고, 이해하지 못한 촌부들은 눈동자를 이리저리 굴리며 작은 목소리로 소곤거렸다.
 74|
 75|“대관절 저게 뭔 뜻이여?”
 76|
 77|“나도 잘 몰러. 관에 속하지 않은 무부는 무림인들을 말하는 것 같긴 한디…… 알아먹기 쉽게 전하면 되지 무슨 말을 저리 거창하게 써 놨대.”
 78|
 79|하루 벌어 하루 먹고 사는 인생.
 80|
 81|태어나 보니 배울 수 있던 것은 몸 쓰는 것과 우직함뿐이라, 늘 가벼운 주머니와 달리 어깨는 천근만근 무거운 그들이 글줄이나 제대로 읽어 보았겠는가.
 82|
 83|하지만 침묵과 무지를 견디지 못하는 이들은 어느 곳에서나 존재하기 마련이었다.
 84|
 85|“폐하께서 친히 내리신 황명이오. 암천의 무리를 역적으로 규정짓는 동시에, 강호의 무림인들과 힘을 합쳐 놈들을 벌할 것을 만백성에게 천명(天命)하신 게지.”
 86|
 87|그제야 사람들의 시선이 밑을 향했다.
 88|
 89|깨알처럼 적힌 글자 아래, 선명하게 찍힌 직인(職印)이 보였다.
 90|
 91|그것은 이 광활한 구주 천하에서 오직 한 존재에게만 허락된, 수많은 이들이 지금껏 본 적도 없었던 옥새의 흔적이었다.
 92|
 93|까막눈들조차 한눈에 범상치 않음을 알아볼 수 있는.
 94|
 95|“예상했던 것보다 사안이 중대하군. 강호인들의 창칼까지 빌려 쓸 정도라니.”
 96|
 97|젊은 유생이 불쑥 꺼낸 그 말에, 또 다른 누군가가 탄식하듯 뇌까렸다.
 98|
 99|“암천에 관한 무성한 소문은 들었지만…… 아무리 그렇다 하여도 이 정도일 줄이야.”
100|
101|천하 각지에서 전해지는 정보를 가장 먼저 듣는 이들은 무림인들과 상계(商界)다.
102|
103|그 밖의 영역에 속한 이들은 따로 연줄이 있지 않고서야 이목이 밝지 않았고, 설령 무슨 일이 터졌다 한들 별다른 걱정을 품지 않았던 것이 현실이었다.
104|
105|단단한 반석 위에 세워진 대국이다.
106|
107|건국 직후 이어졌던 무수한 숙청과 지방 군벌의 반란도 이미 끝난 지 오래.
108|
109|흐르는 시간 속에서 천하는 안정되었고, 무림인들이 정마대전이라 부르는 오십여 년 전의 환란 속에서도 양민들의 피해는 거의 없었다.
110|
111|이유?
112|
113|간단했다.
114|
115|마교(魔敎)라는 섬뜩한 명칭을 지닌, 저 서쪽 너머의 광신도들조차 대국의 참전을 두려워했으니까.
116|
117|단지 강호인들만의 세력 다툼으로 여겨지기를 원했으니까.
118|
119|하지만…….
120|
121|“이번에는 다를 것이오. 그 어느 때와도.”
122|
123|활불(活佛)과도 비견되었던 소림사의 방장이 열반에 들고, 평화로운 목탁 소리만 울려 퍼지던 경내가 피로 물들었을 때만 해도 이중 누구도 안타까움 그 이상의 감정을 느끼지는 않았다.
124|
125|신선과도 같았던 청성과 아미의 도사들이 쓰러지고, 세간에도 독한 놈들이라고 소문난 사천당문이 극심한 피해를 입었다는 소식을 들었어도 마찬가지였다.
126|
127|그것이 모두가 알고 있던 무림(武林)이니까.
128|
129|푸르른 초목 대신 창칼이 난무하는 저 잔인한 숲에서는, 고승도 도사도 언제든지 죽어 나갈 수 있었으니까.
130|
131|아니, 그들이 별다른 걱정 없이 상황을 지켜본 가장 큰 이유는 따로 있었다.
132|
133|‘아무리 그래도 그렇지, 설마하니 우리한테까지 무슨 일이라도 있으려고.’
134|
135|사는 세상이, 울타리가 달랐다.
136|
137|백성들은 대국의 울타리에 몸을 의탁한 채, 자신들만의 영역에서 치열한 전투를 벌이는 무림인들을 지켜보았을 따름이었다.
138|
139|간혹 무림의 일에 휘말려 희생당하는 운 없는 양민들을 안타까워하면서도, 고작 그 정도였다.
140|
141|수백 리 밖에서 불길이 일어나도 그 열기는 모두에게 닿지 않는 법.
142|
143|백성들의 느끼는 감정과 관심은 일순간 뜨겁게 불타올랐다가 빠르게 식었다.
144|
145|전체에 비하면 한 줌에 불과한 극소수의 피해일 뿐, 그들은 멀쩡히 내일을 맞이할 수 있기에.
146|
147|그들에게는 대국이라는 크고 단단한 울타리가 있었기에.
148|
149|그러나 그 굳건한 믿음은, 바로 이 순간 산산이 허물어지고 있었다.
150|
151|“자, 잠깐. 나으리들. 그렇다면 지금 하시는 말씀이 혹시…….”
152|
153|꿀꺽.
154|
155|차마 말을 잇지 못하고 마른침만 삼키는 촌로를 대신하여, 늙은 유생이 입을 열었다.
156|
157|누구도 믿고 싶지도, 듣고 싶지도 않았던.
158|
159|하지만 마주할 수밖에 없는 현실을.
160|
161|“그래. 자네가 생각하는 그것이 맞네.”
162|
163|나직하게 흘러나오는 한숨.
164|
165|늙은 유생은 문득, 세월의 흔적이 아로새겨진 자신의 주름진 손을 내려다보았다.
166|
167|한때는 희고 매끄러웠던, 과거의 모습을 떠올리며.
168|
169|수많은 가능성이 있었음에도 끝나지 않은 난세의 시대에 가로막혀 더는 나아가지 못했던 젊은 날의 자신을, 그 혼란했던 시기를 떠올리며.
170|
171|그는 천천히 말을 이었다.
172|
173|“전란(戰亂)은, 이미 시작되었네.”
174|
175|“……!”
176|
177|“……!”
178|
179|누군가는 이를 악물고 주먹을 쥐었다. 또 다른 눈을 질끈 감았다.
180|
181|소리 없는 경악이 파도가 되어 군중을 휩쓸었다.
182|
183|전란이라는 두 글자가 부릅떠진 눈과 멍하니 벌어진 입술을 통해 사방으로 전해졌다.
184|
185|넓은 대로변에서, 좁고 어두컴컴한 골목길에서, 이 믿을 수 없는 소식을 전하기 위해 바쁘게 움직이는 누군가의 발걸음을 따라서.
186|
187|전쟁.
188|
189|모든 것을 불태울 거대한 대전쟁의 불길.
190|
191|그 순간, 늙은 유생은 보았다.
192|
193|마침내 오랜 세월 잠자고 있던 어둠이 깨어나, 모두의 낯빛을 암담하게 물들이는 것을.
194|
195|그리고 불현듯, 하늘 같은 황명이 적힌 포고문에 등장한 낯선 이름을 조용히 마음속으로 뇌까렸다.
196|
197|태원진가의 진태경.
198|
199|아니, 상산후(上山侯) 진태경.
200|
201|이번의 역모를 막은 일등 공신이자, 젊다 못해 새파란 나이와 무림인이라는 신분임에도 열후(列侯)의 자리에 오른 자.
202|
203|‘비록 강호의 사정에는 밝지 않으나…… 한 가지는 확실하군.’
204|
205|한때 관직에 몸담았던 늙은 유생은 충분히 짐작할 수 있었다.
206|
207|전례(前例)가 없는, 아니 앞으로도 없을 전무후무(前無後無)한 일을 이뤄 낸 저 젊은 무림인을 기다리고 있는 미래를.
208|
209|‘뉘신지는 모르겠으나, 부디 온 힘을 다해 나아가게. 본래 그대가 살아가던 무림을 넘어 이 나라를 위해서라도.’
210|
211|닿지 않을 말과 함께, 늙은 유생은 포고문을 향해 절을 올렸다.
212|
213|첫 번째로는 머나먼 황도에서 모든 것을 굽어보고 있을 천자를 향해.
214|
215|두 번째로는 이 천하를 지키기 위해 피를 흘리며 쓰러질 수많은 영령(英靈)들을 위해.
216|
217|마지막으로, 지엄한 황명으로 무림의 중심에 우뚝 선 새로운 열후를 향해.
218|
219|늙은 유생은 계속해서 절을 올렸다.
220|
221|사람들의 시선 앞에서도 그저 묵묵히, 지금 당장 자신이 할 수 있는 최대한의 예의와 진심을 다하여.
222|
223|그리고 그로부터 수천 리 떨어진 어느 비좁은 협곡에서는, 샛노란 국화꽃이 사방을 물들이고 있었다.
224|
225|
226|
227|* * *
228|
229|
230|
231|나는 중양절(重陽節)에 대해 스치듯 몇 번 들어 보기만 했을 뿐, 그 이상은 알지 못한다.
232|
233|토종 한국인답게 설날과 추석 같은 민족 대표 명절은 꼬박꼬박 챙겼다지만, 대륙 놈들 풍습까지 관심을 가질 정도로 시간이 남아돌지는 않았으니까.
234|
235|그러나 오늘만큼은 나도 중양절의 풍습에 따라 국화꽃을 들었다.
236|
237|샛노란 그것을 넘치도록 한 아름 안고, 산수유가 든 주머니를 어색하게나마 옆구리에 찼다.
238|

## Default

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P38]
They lived from day to day, earning only enough to eat.

[P39]
They had been born with little chance to learn anything but hard work and how to use their bodies. Their pockets were always light, while their shoulders bore the weight of a thousand *geun*. How could they be expected to read a line of writing?

[P40]
But there were always people who couldn’t stand silence or ignorance.

[P41]
“It is an imperial decree personally issued by His Majesty. He has declared Dark Heaven a band of traitors and announced to all his people that he will join forces with the martial artists of the world to punish them.”

[P42]
Only then did people look down.

[P43]
Beneath the tiny letters was a clear imprint of a seal.

[P44]
It was the mark of the imperial seal, reserved for only one person in all the vast Nine Provinces—one that countless people had never even seen.

[P45]
Even those who couldn’t read could tell at a glance that it was no ordinary seal.

[P46]
“This is more serious than I expected. They’re even borrowing the martial world’s swords and spears.”

[P47]
At the young scholar’s sudden remark, someone else murmured with a sigh.

[P48]
“I’ve heard all the rumors about Dark Heaven, but… I never thought it was this bad.”

[P49]
The first to hear news from every corner of the world were martial artists and merchants.

[P50]
People outside those circles rarely had their ear to the ground unless they had special connections. And even when something happened, they generally saw no reason to worry.

[P51]
The Great Nation stood on a firm foundation.

[P52]
The countless purges and provincial warlord rebellions that had followed its founding were long over.

[P53]
With the passage of time, the world had settled into peace. Even during the calamity some fifty years ago that martial artists called the Great Faction War, the common people had suffered almost no harm.

[P54]
Why?

[P55]
It was simple.

[P56]
Even the fanatics from far to the west, who bore the chilling name of the Demonic Cult, had feared the Great Nation joining the war.

[P57]
They had wanted it to be seen as nothing more than a struggle between martial-world factions.

[P58]
But…

[P59]
“This time will be different. Different from any other.”

[P60]
When Shaolin Temple’s Abbot, once likened to a living Buddha, entered nirvana and the grounds where only the peaceful sound of wooden fish had once echoed ran red with blood, no one there had felt anything beyond sorrow.

[P61]
It was the same when they heard that the Daoists of Qingcheng and Emei, who seemed like immortals, had fallen, and that the Sichuan Tang Clan—whose people had a reputation for being a fearsome bunch even among ordinary folk—had suffered terrible losses.

[P62]
That was the Murim everyone knew.

[P63]
In that cruel forest, where spears and swords ran wild in place of green trees, even venerable monks and Daoists could die at any moment.

[P64]
No, there was another reason they had watched it all without much concern.

[P65]
*Whatever happens, surely nothing will happen to us.*

[P66]
They lived in different worlds, behind different walls.

[P67]
The people had entrusted their safety to the Great Nation’s walls. All they had done was watch the martial artists fight their fierce battles in their own domain.

[P68]
Now and then, they pitied the unlucky common folk caught up in Murim affairs and killed. But that was all.

[P69]
A fire blazing hundreds of *ri* away couldn’t warm everyone.

[P70]
The people’s feelings and interest burned hot for a moment, then quickly cooled.

[P71]
Compared to the whole, the victims were only a handful. The rest could wake up tomorrow just fine.

[P72]
They had the Great Nation, a great and sturdy wall.

[P73]
But that unshakable faith was crumbling at that very moment.

[P74]
“W-wait, sirs. Then what you’re saying is…”

[P75]
Gulp.

[P76]
The village elder couldn’t finish. He only swallowed dryly, and the old scholar spoke in his place.

[P77]
He spoke the truth no one wanted to believe or even hear.

[P78]
The truth they had no choice but to face.

[P79]
“That’s right. It’s exactly what you think.”

[P80]
He let out a quiet sigh.

[P81]
The old scholar looked down at his wrinkled hands, etched with the marks of time.

[P82]
He remembered when they had been white and smooth.

[P83]
He remembered his younger self, with so many possibilities before him, unable to go any farther because an age of chaos refused to end. He remembered those turbulent years.

[P84]
Slowly, he continued.

[P85]
“The war has already begun.”

[P86]
“…!”

[P87]
“…!”

[P88]
Some clenched their teeth and fists. Others squeezed their eyes shut.

[P89]
Soundless shock surged through the crowd like a wave.

[P90]
The word *war* spread in every direction, carried in wide-open eyes and slackened lips.

[P91]
Along broad avenues, through narrow, dark alleys, and with the hurried footsteps of those rushing to carry the unbelievable news onward.

[P92]
War.

[P93]
The flames of a great war that would burn everything.

[P94]
At that moment, the old scholar saw it.

[P95]
The darkness that had slumbered for so many years had finally awoken, painting everyone’s faces with despair.

[P96]
And suddenly, he repeated in his mind an unfamiliar name from the proclamation bearing the Son of Heaven’s command.

[P97]
Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.

[P98]
No—the Marquis of Shangshan, Jin Taekyung.

[P99]
The foremost contributor to stopping this rebellion, a martial artist still so young, yet raised to the rank of marquis.

[P100]
*I don’t know much about the affairs of the martial world… but one thing is certain.*

[P101]
The old scholar had once served in government. He could guess well enough what future awaited that young martial artist, who had achieved something without precedent—and something that would never happen again.

[P102]
*I don’t know who you are, but please, give it everything you have and keep moving forward. Not only for the Murim you’ve always known, but for this country as well.*

[P103]
Though his words would never reach him, the old scholar bowed toward the proclamation.

[P104]
First, to the Son of Heaven, who watched over all things from the distant Imperial Capital.

[P105]
Second, to the countless heroic souls who would shed their blood and fall to protect this world.

[P106]
And lastly, to the new marquis who stood at the heart of the martial world by imperial decree.

[P107]
The old scholar continued to bow.

[P108]
In full view of the crowd, he did so silently, offering all the respect and sincerity he could.

[P109]
And thousands of *ri* away, in a narrow gorge, bright yellow chrysanthemums colored the landscape in every direction.

[P110]
* * *

[P111]
I’d heard of the Double Ninth Festival a few times in passing, but that was about all I knew.

[P112]
As a Korean born and raised, I’d always observed the big holidays like Lunar New Year and Chuseok. But I didn’t have so much time on my hands that I could take an interest in the customs of those guys on the continent.

[P113]
Today, though, I followed the customs of the Double Ninth Festival too.

[P114]
I held more bright yellow chrysanthemums than my arms could contain, and awkwardly wore a pouch of cornelian berries at my side.

[P115]
It was only right to honor those who had passed before they could see the Double Ninth Festival.[^1]

[P116]
And we had to keep moving forward, leaving their sacrifice behind us.

[P117]
*Whoosh.*

[P118]
Wind from far away stirred the chrysanthemums in my arms.

[P119]
It came out of nowhere and tugged insistently at them, as if taking them by the hand. Several petals, large and small, gave in and went along with it.

[P120]
Before long, they fluttered through the air like a rain of flowers.

[P121]
Riding the wind, they swam through the twists and turns of the Eight Spring Gorge, as those who had lived on this land long ago had named it.

[P122]
*Ah.*

[P123]
I swallowed the exclamation that almost escaped me.

[P124]
It was beautiful and, at the same time, unbearably sad.

[P125]
I wasn’t the only one who felt it. Tens of thousands of people filled the Eight Spring Gorge, and I knew they felt it too.

[P126]
Watching the yellow petals fall, I found myself wondering. As they drifted farther and farther away with the wind, were they petals? Or were they the souls of those who had willingly given their lives to protect what they cherished?

[P127]
There was no single right answer.

[P128]
There was no need to find one.

[P129]
We could believe what we wanted to believe. We could return to this place someday and remember them.

[P130]
Each in our own way.

[P131]
With laughter. With chrysanthemums and cornelian berries.

[P132]
Or…

[P133]
With tears.

[P134]
Drip. Drip, drip.

[P135]
Senses far beyond human limits sometimes told me things I didn’t want to know.

[P136]
Like the tears wetting the leather shoes of a man who stood with his head bowed, his body trembling slightly.

[P137]
No. Raindrops.

[P138]
*Yeah. That’s how it is.*

[P139]
I quietly looked up at the sky.

[P140]
I couldn’t bring myself to look at Jin Wikyung like that, or at Lee Seowol silently weeping for the uncle who had been her strongest support, or at the countless others.

[P141]
*Whoosh.*

[P142]
The wind blew again.

[P143]
The rain of flowers rose high, then fell around everyone as if to comfort them.

[P144]
Yet beneath a sky clearer than ever, countless raindrops kept falling.

[P145]
The Double Ninth Festival had passed, but the chrysanthemums hadn’t withered.

[P146]
I knew that those who had left and those who remained were all here together.

[P147]
And I knew that because of them, the road ahead had grown wider and brighter.

[P148]
*Ding.*

[P149]
A clear chime rang through the sky, mingling with the rain of flowers.
